## 2. Findings

### Medium

**CR-01 - Nothing has been executed; dependency pins unverified on Python 3.14** (`requirements.txt`, `tests/*`)
- Both the app and the 90-odd test assertions are unrun, so import errors, template syntax errors, or fragile tests would only show up in Step 7. `Flask==3.1.3`, `Werkzeug==3.1.9`, `pytest==9.2.0` are the latest releases listed by `pip index` but have not been installed on Python 3.14. `app/db.py` also imports `click` directly, but it is only a transitive dependency of Flask and is not pinned.
- *Recommendation:* Step 7 installs into a fresh venv and runs `pytest` first. Add `click` to `requirements.txt` only if the Flask install does not pin a compatible version (harmless to add). One test, `test_sql_metacharacters_are_inert`, passes a raw query string with spaces and a quote in the URL; use `query_string={"q": ...}` to avoid client-side URL parsing differences.

### Low

**CR-02 - No handler for 405 (and CSRF runs before routing 404/405).** `ERROR_MESSAGES` in `app/__init__.py` omits 405, so e.g. `GET /auth/logout` returns Werkzeug's unstyled default page (headers are still applied). A POST to a non-existent URL returns 400 (CSRF) instead of 404 because `security.before_request` runs when `request.endpoint` is `None`. *Fix:* add a 405 entry; skip the CSRF check when `request.endpoint is None`.

**CR-03 - Search term has no server-side length cap** (`app/blog.py:index`). `maxlength="100"` exists only in the HTML. A long `q` (bounded only by the server's URL limit) makes SQLite scan with a large pattern. *Fix:* `query = query[:100]`.

**CR-04 - Create and edit duplicate their validate/render logic** (`app/blog.py`). Both handlers read `title`/`content`, validate, and render the form with errors in near-identical code. *Fix:* extract a small `_read_post_form()` helper returning `(title, content, errors)`. No behavior change.

**CR-05 - Module constant name shadows Flask config meaning** (`app/blog.py`). `MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH = 10_000` (characters per post) has the same name as the Flask config key `MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH` (bytes per request, 64 KB), which invites confusion. *Fix:* rename to `MAX_POST_CONTENT_CHARS` and `MAX_POST_TITLE_CHARS`.

**CR-06 - Template filter registered in `security.py`** (`app/security.py:init_app`). `format_timestamp` is presentation logic unrelated to security. *Fix:* move it to `app/__init__.py` or a small `filters` section in `blog.py` (register via `app.template_filter`).

**CR-07 - Content is stripped on both sides** (`app/blog.py`). `.strip()` removes leading indentation on the first line of a post, which matters little for plain text but is a silent change to user input. *Fix:* validate on the stripped value but store only `rstrip()`ed content, or accept and document. Low priority.

**CR-08 - Debug mode uses a hard-coded fallback `SECRET_KEY`** (`app/__init__.py`). With `FLASK_DEBUG=1` and no `SECRET_KEY`, sessions are signed with a publicly known string. Acceptable for local development and documented in the README, but it would be forgeable if someone ran debug mode on a reachable host. *Fix:* generate `secrets.token_hex(32)` per process instead (sessions then reset on restart, which is fine in development).

**CR-09 - Test gaps.** No tests for: the session-expired flash message, a registration success flash, `GET /auth/logout` (405), the `init-db` CLI command, or `static/app.js` behavior (auto-submit on sort change, keep-alive timer). The JS cannot be covered by the Flask test client. *Fix:* add the two or three trivial Flask-client tests; verify JS manually in Step 7 (or note it as untested).

## 3. Requirements Conformance

| Story | Result | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| US-101 Registration | Pass | `auth.register`; client attributes in `register.html`; server validation; duplicate checks (case-insensitive); redirect to Login |
| US-102 Login | Pass | `auth.login`; username or email; generic 401 message; redirect to `/` |
| US-103 Session & Logout | Pass | Signed cookie persists across requests; POST logout button in nav; `security.before_request` enforces 30-minute inactivity |
| US-201 Feed | Pass | `blog.index` lists all users' posts with title, author, modified date, snippet; link to detail |
| US-202 Search | Pass | `q` on title/content, case-insensitive for ASCII, empty state "No blogs found" |
| US-203 Sort | Pass | Four whitelisted options, applied on select change or Search click |
| US-301 Create | Pass | Login required; Title/Content; author from session; redirect to new post |
| US-302 Edit | Pass | Edit link author-only; pre-populated form; `updated_at` set; 403 for others (GET and POST) |
| US-303 Delete | Pass | Delete link author-only; server-rendered confirmation page; POST removes; 403 for others |
| NFR-01 to NFR-05 | Pass | Minimal UI, no frameworks; hashed passwords; RBAC; 30-minute timeout; out-of-scope features absent |

Design-review amendments verified in code: F-01 (`USERNAME_RE` forbids `@`; `_find_user` branches on `@`), F-02 (keep-alive route + `app.js`), F-03 (delete confirm page), F-04 (`MAX_PASSWORD_LENGTH`, `MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH`), F-05 (env-driven cookie flag), F-06 (headers in `after_request`), F-07 (`run.py`), F-08/F-09 (lowercased email, ASCII constraint, fixed-width timestamps, tiebreakers), F-11 (single GET form), F-12 (lazy token, `compare_digest`), F-13 (dummy hash), F-14 (strip/validate), F-15 (`.gitignore`, `init-db`, `<int:post_id>`).

## 4. Security Review

| Area | Assessment |
|---|---|
| SQL injection | Good: all values parameterized; the only interpolated SQL fragments are the whitelisted `ORDER BY` string and constant column list. |
| XSS | Good: autoescape on, no `|safe`, CSP `default-src 'self'` blocks inline script, no inline handlers or styles in templates. |
| CSRF | Good: every POST (including logout, delete, keep-alive) checked with constant-time compare. |
| Authz | Good: `_get_owned_post` returns 404 then 403 before any mutation; `login_required` precedes ownership. |
| Authn | Good: scrypt via Werkzeug, dummy-hash timing parity, session rebuilt on login, max password length. |
| Session | Good with known limits (stateless, non-revocable cookie; accepted as F-10). |
| Secrets | Good: no secrets in repo; `.gitignore` covers `instance/`, `*.db`, `.env`. See CR-08 for the debug-mode fallback. |
| Info leakage | Good: generic error pages, no stack traces outside debug mode. |

## 5. Code Quality Notes

- **Clarity:** modules are small and single-purpose; names are descriptive; comments are limited to the non-obvious (sort whitelist, dummy hash, patchable clock).
- **DRY:** only CR-04 (create/edit) and the repeated `render_template("blog/form.html", ...)` argument lists stand out; the test suite has some repetition that is acceptable for readability.
- **Error handling:** appropriate at boundaries (form input, IntegrityError race on registration, oversized body). No speculative handling found.
- **Watermark:** verified on all 27 generated files in the correct comment syntax for each file type.
